title: Sell Mineral Rights in Plumerville, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Plumerville, AR
metaDescription: Plumerville, AR mineral rights in Conway County's Fayetteville Shale trend, near I-40 and the Arkansas River valley. Legacy 2000s-era gas leases.
heroLead: Plumerville sits along the Arkansas River valley in Conway County, where Fayetteville Shale leasing moved through farmland during the mid-2000s alongside the interstate corridor.
intro: The land around Plumerville was part of the broader Conway County leasing wave tied to the Fayetteville Shale boom, though as in much of the county's western portion, drilling density varied significantly from one tract to the next. Mineral ownership here tends to run in families who farmed the river valley for generations before the shale play ever arrived.

sections.heading: River Valley Farmland, Shale-Era Leases
paragraphs: Farmland along the Arkansas River valley near Plumerville was leased for gas rights the same way as the rest of Conway County during the boom, with the mineral estate treated separately from the surface farming operation that continued on top of it. Some of those leases resulted in producing wells, while others lapsed as drilling activity slowed after 2012.

sections.heading: What's Needed to Confirm Your Interest
paragraphs: The Conway County Circuit Clerk's office in Morrilton holds the deed, probate, and lease records relevant to any Plumerville-area tract. If your interest passed through inheritance, a title check will confirm whether the estate was formally probated or whether an affidavit of heirship is needed to clear up ownership before a sale.

faqs.question: Does farming the surface affect who owns the mineral rights near Plumerville?
faqs.answer: No, the two are typically separate. A family can continue farming the surface while the mineral rights are leased, sold, or held independently by them or a previous owner.

faqs.question: Is my old Conway County lease still valid if I haven't received a check in years?
faqs.answer: That depends on whether it's being held by production from a well elsewhere in the unit or has expired. A records check will confirm which applies to your tract.

faqs.question: How do I get started if I only have an old paper lease with faded print?
faqs.answer: Send what you have. Even a partial or hard-to-read document usually contains enough information, like names or a legal description, to look up the current records.

faqs.question: Does river valley farmland typically carry different mineral value than upland tracts nearby?
faqs.answer: Not inherently. Value comes from a tract's position within the underlying gas play and its lease status, not from surface characteristics like farmland versus timber or upland terrain.

faqs.question: Can I sell my Plumerville-area interest while continuing to farm the surface?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mineral rights and surface farming operations are independent, so selling the minerals doesn't affect your continued use of the land above them.
